title: Id segments portable
description: Outside the @context, every @id with no colon before its first /, ? or # is a path of portable segments: each segment holds only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores -- the POSIX portable filename character set -- and begins and ends with a letter or digit. The named denials below say the same thing of the mistakes a producer is likeliest to make, so that the message names the mistake rather than the pattern.
summary: Every segment of a relative `@id` is a portable name: letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores, beginning and ending with a letter or digit

errorMessage.not: a relative @id does not begin with /
a relative @id does not begin with @
a relative @id has no . or .. segments
a relative @id has no empty segment

errorMessage.pattern: a segment of a relative @id holds only letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores, and begins and ends with a letter or digit
